---
title: "Is Karlsruhe Getting Sunnier?"
subtitle: "Annual sunshine hours since the 1930s"
author: "Solution to the c03 Try-it"
date: today
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
if (!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman")
p_load(tidyverse, tinytable)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr file.mtime("data/weather_karlsruhe.csv")
sunshine_yearly <- read_csv("data/weather_karlsruhe.csv") |>
  mutate(year = year(date)) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarize(
    days_measured = sum(!is.na(sunshine)),
    sunshine = sum(sunshine, na.rm = TRUE),
    station = last(station)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(days_measured >= 360)
```

```{r}
#| label: key-numbers
sunshine_periods <- sunshine_yearly |>
  mutate(
    period = case_when(
      year %in% 1961:1990 ~ "reference",
      year %in% 1996:2025 ~ "recent"
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(period)) |>
  group_by(period) |>
  summarize(sunshine = mean(sunshine)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = sunshine)

sunshine_reference <- sunshine_periods |>
  pull(reference) |>
  round()

sunshine_gain <- sunshine_periods |>
  mutate(gain = recent - reference) |>
  pull(gain) |>
  round()

first_year <- sunshine_yearly |>
  summarize(start = min(year)) |>
  pull(start)
```

## Question and data

Sunshine matters for agriculture, solar power and health, and it isn't constant: across Europe,
sunshine at the surface fell from the 1950s to the 1980s and has risen since, a pattern known as
"dimming" and "brightening" [@wild2009]. Does Karlsruhe show it too?

The data are daily sunshine hours from the Deutscher Wetterdienst [@dwd2026], from the
Karlsruhe station until 2008 and from Rheinstetten since, analysed with the tidyverse
[@wickham2023]. Sunshine was measured from `r first_year` on. We only keep years with at least
360 measured days.

## Results

@fig-sunshine shows the annual sunshine hours. After a dip to the 1970s, the trend points
clearly upwards: in 1996–2025, Karlsruhe had `r sunshine_gain` more hours of sunshine per year
than in the reference period 1961–1990 (`r sunshine_reference` hours).

```{r}
#| label: fig-sunshine
#| fig-cap: "Annual sunshine hours, with a smoothed trend."
sunshine_yearly |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = sunshine)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = station)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Karlsruhe = "#F1C232", Rheinstetten = "#E69138")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1200, NA)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Sunshine (hours per year)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

@tbl-decades gives the averages per decade.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-decades
#| tbl-cap: "Average annual sunshine hours per decade (complete years only)."
sunshine_yearly |>
  mutate(decade = str_c(year %/% 10 * 10, "s")) |>
  group_by(decade) |>
  summarize(
    sunshine = mean(sunshine),
    years = n()
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  rename(
    Decade = decade,
    `Sunshine (hours)` = sunshine,
    Years = years
  ) |>
  tt() |>
  format_tt(digits = 0, num_fmt = "decimal")
```

## Conclusion

Yes: Karlsruhe has been getting sunnier since the 1980s, after a darker period in the 1960s and
1970s, in line with the European dimming and brightening. One caveat: the series switches from
the Karlsruhe to the Rheinstetten station in 2008, so part of a difference across that year
could come from the change of location.
